user_msg: Independently inspect this claim: 'a portable self-orch rail can run five GLM seats and one Grok seat in true parallel, returning one terminal substrate_group.' Each seat has a unique angle. Do not copy each other. Be concrete and short (≤120 words).

seats.query_angle: how this parallel dispatch can fail
seats.brief: Name 5 concrete failure modes of a 6-seat parallel HTTP parliament (timeouts, empty reasoning-only responses, key routing, partial completion). No fluff.
State the governor-facing contract in 6 bullets: blocking call, dispatch_state values, final-text-only, no agent launch, max seats, keys-from-env. Attack any ambiguity.
Explain how glm* vs grok* prefixes must route to different providers. What happens if a grok seat is sent to the GLM endpoint? One paragraph.
Specify a stderr-only live panel so stdout remains parseable JSON. 5 lines of requirements a TTY dashboard must meet.
How a terminal agent with no Aurelius MCP uses this CLI. Name the files it should read (SKILL.md, AGENTS.md) and the single command it runs.
You are the Grok seat. Judge whether five GLM + one Grok in one dispatch is a valid test of the rail. Verdict: HOLD | PARTIAL | FAIL, then 4 sentences of why. Try to disprove the claim if you can.
